title: Station Cobb Salad
shortDescription: Chopped salad with chicken, bacon, egg, and blue cheese for ten
subtitle: Chopped salad with chicken, bacon, egg, and blue cheese for ten
description: Grilled chicken, crisp bacon, hard-boiled eggs, avocado, and blue cheese top chopped romaine in rows for a classic Cobb spread. Crews build bowls at the line with ranch or vinaigrette.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Station Cobb Salad in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.instruction: Season chicken breasts and grill or sear over medium-high heat 6–7 minutes per side until internal temp reaches 165°F. Rest and slice. Target oven/smoker temperature: 165°F.

steps.title: Crisp the bacon
steps.instruction: Bake bacon on sheet pans at 400°F until crisp, about 15 minutes. Drain on paper towels and crumble. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Prep the components
steps.instruction: Hard-boil eggs 10 minutes, ice bath, peel and quarter. Chop romaine and wash tomatoes. Slice avocados just before assembly. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.instruction: Whisk vinegar, Dijon, salt, and pepper, then stream in olive oil until emulsified. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Station Cobb Salad onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Assemble and serve
steps.instruction: Spread romaine on platters. Arrange chicken, bacon, eggs, avocado, tomatoes, and blue cheese in rows. Serve dressing on the side. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Rotisserie chicken works in a pinch if grill time is tight—season with extra pepper.
Red onion slices add bite—soak in cold water 5 minutes if raw onion runs strong.
Grilled corn kernels mixed in turn this into a summer station favorite.
tonightSpread: Cobb platters with dressing choice and warm dinner rolls.
Fresh fruit bowl for crew who want something sweet after the meal.
leftovers: Pack components separately—do not dress until eating or salad turns soggy.
Chop leftovers into a wrap with ranch for quick lunch.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Salad night does not have to feel like punishment when there is bacon, egg, and grilled chicken in the mix. The row presentation looks sharp for visiting crews and photos.
mealPrepNotes: Cook chicken and bacon ahead. Hard-boil eggs ice-bath immediately for clean peels. Keep avocado sliced just before service to prevent browning.
